summary: Daily investment refresh: no new stock cleared the promotion bar. Unitree's Shanghai debut (+~460% close versus IPO price) strengthens the robotics-capital/adoption signal but makes the OEM unattractive to chase; the commercialization hierarchy remains warehouse/fixed automation, cobots/mobile manipulation, industrial humanoids, then general-purpose humanoids. Texas's data-centre audit is now treated as a cross-stack power/water/cooling constraint because projects must disclose grid dependence, on-site generation, water sourcing/reuse and cooling technology, reinforcing existing integrated grid/cooling/water exposures without adding a duplicate ticker. Brent settled at $91.62 and WTI $85.83 with Hormuz uncertainty; crude inventories rose but refinery utilisation/product tightness preserve the tactical refining thesis. China's nuclear buildout remains supported by eight newly approved reactors and Taipingling 2 commercial operation. July ISM remains the latest official dataset and was re-verified without timestamp churn. Added data/powerstack-update-2026-08-20.json; no UI, scoring, automation or backend changes.

Macro Pulse v2: verified the deployed Macro Indicators dashboard source semantics, then replaced theme-level stock scoring with stock-specific macro fingerprints. Added raw-measurement guardrails for CPI/PCE, yields, calendar surprises and already-transformed series; split broad credit from tail credit stress and crude from refined-product/gas tightness. Added 49 stock sensitivity profiles with 65% fundamental / 35% market weighting, confidence/freshness scaling, zero adjustment when stale/unprofiled, and a ±1.00 cap. Base Conviction values were not changed.

Replaced the active Live Desk Pulse with a macro-regime Pulse. Power Stack now reads data/macro-context.json, built from a reviewed scan of the Macro Indicators dashboard across Growth, Inflation, Labour, Rates, Credit, Consumer, Housing, Energy and Positioning, then translates that regime into all current Power Stack themes. Live Desk influence is zero and its scheduled sync is disabled but retained as a dormant stub. Base Conviction remains untouched; macro adjustment is transparent, stale-safe and capped at +/-1.00. No stock research scores were changed in this implementation commit.

Daily investment refresh: promoted BHP Group ADR (BHP) at 8.1 as a diversified Metals crossover after FY2026 results confirmed copper now generates roughly 55% of underlying EBITDA and has overtaken iron ore as the largest earnings contributor. Jansen adds potash/food-security exposure from 2027 and Olympic Dam adds uranium by-product optionality. Power/Grid remains the core category, but 30-year Treasury yields at their highest since 2007 and Brent above $91 increase valuation pressure on long-duration AI/infrastructure names. Water/Cooling, Agriculture, Healthcare/Metabolic and Robotics rankings were unchanged. July ISM remains the latest official dataset and was re-verified without timestamp churn. Added data/metals-research.json and data/powerstack-update-2026-08-19.json; no UI, scoring, automation or backend changes.

Daily investment refresh: promoted NexGen Energy (NXE) to 8.3 as the preferred higher-beta development-stage uranium satellite after Rook I final construction approval, construction commencement and reported BHP strategic-financing discussions materially improved project validation. CCJ remains the core uranium/Westinghouse exposure and LEU the strategic U.S. enrichment scarcity play. Power/Grid remains the highest-conviction category; Water/Cooling remains the strongest new diversification sleeve led by ECL/MOD/XYL; Agriculture and Healthcare/Metabolic rankings were unchanged. Brent moved back above $90 and long-end Treasury yields rose sharply, increasing both geopolitical-hedge value in energy and valuation pressure on long-duration equities. July ISM remains the latest official dataset and was re-verified without timestamp churn. Added data/uranium-research.json and data/powerstack-update-2026-08-18.json; no UI, scoring, automation or backend changes.

Daily investment refresh: re-screened the full tracked universe after the Water/Cooling, Agriculture/Food Systems and Healthcare/Metabolic expansion. No additional ticker cleared the promotion bar. Power/Grid remains the strongest core category; Water/Cooling is now an overweight emerging bottleneck led by ECL/MOD/XYL. Hormuz shipping slowed sharply with Brent near $89, strengthening oil/refining as a tactical hedge while weak demand signals keep the crude thesis two-sided. Robotics adoption order remains warehouse/fixed automation first despite extreme Unitree IPO demand. July ISM remains the latest official dataset and was re-verified without timestamp churn. Live Desk theme states remain stale/neutral, so no score changes were driven by the overlay. Added data/powerstack-update-2026-08-17.json; no UI, scoring, automation or backend changes.

Expanded the personal-investment universe with three first-class themes: Water / Cooling, Agriculture / Food Systems, and Healthcare / Metabolic. Added Ecolab (ECL) 8.9 for industrial/ultrapure water plus CoolIT direct liquid cooling, Modine (MOD) 8.6 for hyperscale data-centre thermal management, Xylem (XYL) 8.5 for water infrastructure/reuse, Valmont (VMI) 8.1 for irrigation/water-efficiency plus grid crossover, Corteva (CTVA) 8.0 for seed/crop-protection productivity, Eli Lilly (LLY) 8.7 for obesity/type-2 diabetes therapeutics, and Dexcom (DXCM) 8.2 for continuous glucose monitoring and metabolic-health biosensing. Kept LNN, NTR and BG on lower-priority watch due current cyclicality/volume/margin considerations. Existing Vertiv remains a core data-centre cooling exposure.

Daily investment refresh: promoted Powell Industries (POWL) at 8.2 as a differentiated switchgear/engineered power-distribution bottleneck after exceptional order/backlog momentum cleared the quality bar. Power/Grid remains the strongest category and the preference for equipment/T&D over indiscriminate merchant-generation beta was reinforced. Copper supply sensitivity strengthened after DRC concentrate disruption, but no miner was added. Robotics adoption order remains warehouse/fixed automation first; July ISM remains the latest official release and was re-verified without timestamp-only churn. No site code, scoring, automation or backend changes.

Promoted SYM, Geekplus, Cognex, Teradyne, UBTECH, Tesla, UiPath, Cloudflare and SpaceX into the visible Power Stack universe with complete risk meters; kept SERV, SoftBank/ABB, Unitree, ICE, S&P Global, Visa, Mastercard, Micron and Nvidia out where economics, valuation evidence or thematic fit did not clear the bar. Personal-investment use only; no scoring or backend logic changes.

Kept SpaceX as a dedicated investment research candidate rather than forcing it into one Power Stack category; stored its Starlink/AI-compute/lockup thesis separately for portfolio research.

Updated macro stance for softer CPI but still-elevated oil and yields.

Added transparent per-idea Live Desk rationale: individual signal contributions, base vs context-adjusted conviction, stale-context gating, and contradiction/research-trigger watch items.
